name: KurrentDB (EventStoreDB)
tagline: A purpose-built event store for event sourcing, with streams, subscriptions and projections.
description: KurrentDB, called EventStoreDB until the company rebranded as Kurrent in late 2024, is a database built for event sourcing: data is appended as immutable events to millions of fine-grained streams, with optimistic concurrency per stream, catch-up and persistent subscriptions, and server-side projections. Recent versions add connectors to Kafka, MongoDB, Elasticsearch and relational sinks, plus SQL access over Arrow Flight. It is the reference store for CQRS/event-sourced systems in .NET and JVM shops. Licensing tightened with 26.2 (2026): single-node production use stays free, but clustering, read-only replicas, archiving and encryption at rest now require an Enterprise license.

pricing.notes: Single-node use free under KLv1; clustering and enterprise features need a license key; Kurrent Cloud is a managed option.

scale.notes: Clusters replicate the full log to every node for availability rather than sharding; 26.2 moves clustering to Raft.

strengths: Built for event sourcing: per-stream optimistic concurrency and ordering
Catch-up and persistent subscriptions make building read models straightforward
Immutable log gives a natural audit trail and replay
First-party connectors to Kafka, MongoDB, Elasticsearch and SQL databases
Mature clients for .NET, JVM, Node.js, Go, Python and Rust
weaknesses: Clustering and encryption at rest now require a paid license (26.2+)
No sharding; one cluster's write throughput is bounded by a single leader
Not suited to ad-hoc querying of current state
Source-available license, not OSI open source
useCases: Integrating microservices via durable event streams
notIdealFor: General CRUD apps without event-sourcing needs
High-volume telemetry better suited to Kafka or time-series DBs
